w10_T4_000565: A publisher prepared 200 titles for a new series, and each title has 9 chapters. Every chapter carries 2 illustrations. The art editor added 68 cover illustrations to the same archive, then cut 623 pictures that were too similar to one another. For the second printing the whole archive was reproduced once more alongside the originals, so it ended up holding 2 times as many illustrations as before. How many illustrations are in the archive now?
w10_T4_000569: On Tuesday morning a car wash had 159 bookings on the sheet, and 9 more were phoned in before the gates opened. Every booking takes 9 minutes of machine time. Later that morning the work was split equally among the site's 3 lanes. In the afternoon lane one picked up an extra 40 minutes of work, and in the evening another 30 minutes were added to that lane. The water company charges 6 cents for each minute a lane runs. The site has 12 parking bays. The bill is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does lane one cost to run?
w10_T4_000573: A community fridge held 93 ready meals on Monday morning, and 66 were taken during the day. A supermarket then delivered 70 more, and 69 were collected by families that evening. A second fridge was filled to match the first, so the scheme held twice as many meals as it had before. A lunch club used 41 of the meals, and a caterer donated 56. The volunteers' rota is written in minutes rather than in hours. How many meals does the scheme have?
w10_T4_000577: Ravi ordered 16 sheets of plywood for a shelving job and sent 4 back because they had warped. His workmate Dana, who ordered fewer sheets than Ravi did, cut every good sheet into 8 shelves. Each shelf was then drilled with 3 fixing holes. The workshop wall already had 15 holes drilled for the same job, and the second wall had 29. A dozen clamps hang on the rail by the door. How many fixing holes are there for the job altogether?
w10_T4_000580: A youth theatre had 51 scripts in the office and the writer printed 54 more. A local school lent the group 60 scripts, and the library donated 38. 174 scripts went out to the cast and crew for rehearsals, and 19 were lost somewhere backstage. A dozen chairs were set out for the first read-through. The rehearsal schedule is written in minutes rather than in hours. How many scripts are left in the office?
w10_T4_000584: On Saturday morning a market gardener cut 176 bunches of flowers, and her helper Tom cut 37 more, fewer than she had managed herself. During the afternoon every bunch on the bench was tied with 4 stems of foliage. In the early evening a florist dropped off 32 spare stems and a neighbour brought 21 more. A late order then took 105 stems away. How many stems of foliage are left?
w10_T4_000587: A podcast studio had 220 minutes of tape in the cupboard and bought 59 minutes more. The first episode used up 160 minutes. The studio then recorded a duplicate of everything it had left, so the cupboard held 2 times as many minutes as before. Every minute of tape was copied onto 7 discs, and each disc was burned 2 times over for the archive. The studio log is kept in minutes rather than in hours. How many disc burns were made?
w10_T4_000590: Priya's orchard has 95 apple trees, and every tree carries 7 fruiting branches. Each branch holds 6 clusters, and every cluster has 8 apples on it. Her neighbour Otis, who tends fewer trees than Priya does, added 43 apples from his own tree to her crop. Each apple in the crop will be pressed into 5 spoonfuls of sauce. A dozen ladders lean against the barn wall. How many spoonfuls of sauce will the crop make?
w10_T4_000592: A tannery cut 37 hides, and every hide was divided into 8 panels. Each panel was then split into 2 strips, and every strip was stamped with 5 metal studs. A quality check afterwards found 1677 studs that had worked loose, and all of those were taken out. The tannery yard is 40 metres long. How many studs are still in place?
w10_T4_000593: A community choir sold 238 tickets for its winter run in the first week. The corner shop sold another 21, the website took 38, the box office sold 64 on the door, and a coach party bought 44. The ticket holders were then divided equally among the 3 evenings of the run. A dozen singers stand in the front row. How many ticket holders are booked for one evening?
w10_T4_000594: A school stationery cupboard held 223 folders at the start of term, and 110 of them went out to the new intake. 24 folders came back unused the following week. Each folder in the cupboard was filled with 4 workbooks, and every workbook contains 7 exercises. A dozen spare pens sit on the shelf beside them. How many exercises are there in the workbooks?
w10_T4_000596: On Thursday morning a fishmonger took delivery of 29 boxes of sardines, with 5 trays packed in every box. During the afternoon he counted 8 fish on each tray. In the evening a late delivery added 16 more fish to the counter, and by closing time 1043 fish had been sold. A dozen cats waited by the back door. The price board is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many fish are left on the counter?
w10_T4_000597: On Monday morning a physiotherapy clinic had 146 minutes of appointments in the diary, and the receptionist added 10 more before opening and another 25 at nine o'clock. The insurer pays 5 cents for every booked minute. In the afternoon it allowed a further 51 cents for equipment, and the second therapist, Noor, who sees fewer patients than her colleague Ilya, added 70 cents of materials to the claim. In the evening a late case added 8 cents. The claim form is filled in in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents does the claim come to?
w10_T4_000604: Mira's allotment shed held 121 flower pots until 26 of them cracked in the frost. Her plot neighbour Tomas, who keeps fewer pots than Mira does, gave her 60 of his. She lent 84 pots to the school gardening club for the summer. She then bought 23 pots at a car boot sale and was given 39 by the garden centre. A dozen robins hopped about the plot while she stacked them. How many pots does Mira have?
w10_T4_000611: A community hall had 177 notice boards in storage, and 45 of them were carried over to the annexe. The caretaker unscrewed all 6 screws from every board still in the hall. He sorted the loose screws into bags of 6, filling every bag completely. Each full bag was then closed with 4 staples. A dozen mops stood in the store cupboard. How many staples did the caretaker use?
w10_T4_000613: A model shop had 120 kits on the shelf and a supplier sent 37 more before the holidays. Every kit contains 7 painted figures. Customers bought 984 figures over the season. A cancelled order then put 53 figures back on the shelf. How many figures are on the shelf now?
w10_T4_000617: On Sunday morning a museum shop had 45 packs of postcards, and 20 packs were sold before lunch. In the early afternoon the assistant counted 8 postcards inside each pack that was left. Later that afternoon a school group bought 180 postcards, and the stockroom sent up 41 more. In the evening 43 postcards went out in a mail order, and the manager found 4 on the counter and put them back with the rest. A dozen umbrellas stood in the stand by the door. How many postcards does the shop have?
w10_T4_000622: A charity's collection round covers 15 streets, and each street has 8 houses that give every year. Every one of those houses drops 4 coins into the tin, and each coin is worth 5 cents. A supporter then posted 53 cents through the office door. The round is 3 kilometres long. The total is counted in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents were collected?
w10_T4_000624: A bulb merchant planted 96 trays with 8 bulbs in every tray. 23 of the bulbs rotted in the wet spring and were dug out. A supplier sent 44 replacement bulbs, and a customer returned 61 that were never planted. The spring sale then sold 604 bulbs. How many bulbs does the merchant still have?
w10_T4_000630: On Saturday morning Amos had 43 kites on his stall and a supplier brought 19 more. Before noon the wind damaged 4 of them beyond repair. In the afternoon he split the stall's kites equally with his partner Rosa, so each of them had the same number to sell, though Rosa sold hers more slowly than Amos did. In the early evening Amos sold 17 of his own kites. He then tied 9 metres of string to every kite he had left. How many metres of string did Amos use?
w10_T4_000631: Kwame pressed 108 sheets of stamps, with 8 stamps on every sheet, and his colleague Ada, who presses fewer sheets than Kwame does, added 71 loose stamps to the same batch. Every stamp in the batch was perforated with 8 tiny holes. Each hole was then checked 2 times over by the inspection machine. The inspector recorded 1717 of those checks as failures. How many checks passed?
w10_T4_000635: Lena's mill runs 137 looms, and each loom holds 6 reels of thread. Every reel is wound from 5 spools. A supplier sent 77 spare spools to the mill, and 22 spools arrived damaged and were thrown away. Each spool carries 8 lengths of thread, and every length is folded 6 times before packing. Lena's partner Georg runs fewer looms than she does at his own mill across the valley. How many folds are made in the mill's thread?
w10_T4_000638: On Monday morning a bike courier set off with 135 envelopes and delivered 39 of them before ten o'clock. Before lunch a further 71 were dropped off on the second run. In the afternoon he found that every envelope still in his bag holds 7 documents. In the evening 34 of those documents were pulled out as duplicates, and each document that was left had to be stamped 4 times. How many stamps did the courier make?
w10_T4_000640: A tram driver logged 19 trips last week, and each trip included 5 minutes of idling at the terminus. A new signal cut 26 of those minutes from the week, a rescheduled stop saved 46 more, and a quicker turnaround saved a further 4. The depot is charged 9 cents for every minute a tram spends idling. The bill is written in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents was the depot charged?
w10_T4_000643: A craft fair organiser had 122 stall passes and printed 63 more before the weekend. Each pass admits 7 people to the hall. The exhibitors themselves took up 1156 of those places. A late cancellation returned 46 places to the pool, then a school group claimed 51, and a sponsor released 70 more places to the public. A dozen stewards worked the entrance. How many places are still available?
